newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Aug 1.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- Despite good remarks from political groups, a survey showed Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa's reputation and the people's trust in him had come down since the handover.

-- SING TAO -- Beijing's Foreign Ministry Commissioner in Hong Kong, Ma Yuzhen, said the Commission had set up a complete communication system with the Hong Kong government, and he would talk directly with Chief Executive Tung over important issues.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Despite the recent outbreak of crime and a bomb explosion outside the Governor's Palace in Macau, the Macau Governor insisted the Portuguese-run enclave's social security was not too bad and people were safe walking in the streets.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin on the 70th anniversary of People's Liberation Army stressed the army's ability to safeguard unification and security and said important strategic plans would be laid out at the 15th Party Congress.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- The market value of the Hong Kong stock exchange reached US$551 billion at the end of June, making the market the sixth biggest in the world. It had surged by 7.4 per cent since the handover.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Chief Executive Tung hinted on a plan to reduce taxes in the face of Hong Kong's huge fiscal surplus. He said studies were under way on how to use the HK$350 billion surplus to enhance Hong Kong's competitiveness.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Stock Exchange Chief Executive Alec Tsui hit back at comments by Security and Futures Commission chairman Anthony Neoh labelling the stock market as the "Wild West of the East".
